metaDescription: Seven wet dry shop vacs compared on tank size, peak horsepower versus airflow, hose diameter, filter type, blower port and portability for garages.
expertTake: The DEWALT 9 gallon wet dry vac with a blower port is our top pick for a durable build, a useful tank size and attachments that cover most garage jobs. The Armor All 2.5 gallon is the value pick for a tiny, light vac for the car and small messes. Skip a bigger tank for the sake of the horsepower number, because peak horsepower is a marketing figure and real suction depends on airflow and the hose, not the label.
introParagraphs: A wet dry shop vac sucks up sawdust, water, debris and spills that would destroy a household vacuum. It is a basic tool for any garage or workshop, and it can double as a blower on models with an exhaust port.

The labels shout horsepower and gallons, but the useful numbers are airflow, hose size, filter quality and how the tank empties. We evaluated seven models from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, then ranked them by fit for garage, workshop and car use, not by the biggest peak horsepower figure.

products.name: DEWALT 9 gallon wet dry vac, heavy duty, 5 peak HP, attachments, blower function
products.description:
The DEWALT 9 gallon vac has a 5 peak horsepower motor, a blower port and a set of attachments in a heavy duty build. Nine gallons is large enough for a garage clean up yet small enough to move easily.

Peak horsepower is a measure taken with no load and says little about real suction, so judge the machine by hose size, filter and owner feedback instead. The blower port helps with leaves, dust and drying wet surfaces. Against the CRAFTSMAN 9 gallon, the DEWALT has a higher peak figure and a tougher brand image. Against the Shop-Vac 8 gallon, it has a similar size and a stronger build.

Empty the tank after each use and check the filter. Use a bag for fine dust to protect the filter and the motor. Owners often say the attachments are what make a shop vac useful, since a floor tool and a crevice tool turn it from a bucket with a motor into a proper cleaner.
products.bestFor: Garage and job site cleanup that needs a durable all rounder.

Blower port adds leaf and drying uses
Attachments cover floors, crevices and corners
Durable build from a tool brand
cons: Peak horsepower is a marketing number
Upper price tier compared with basic vacs
Hose diameter is standard, not wide

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17595 16 gallon 6.5 peak HP wet dry shop vacuum, heavy duty
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN 16 gallon vac has a 6.5 peak horsepower motor and a big tank for large jobs such as a flooded basement, a full workshop clean up or construction debris. The bigger tank means fewer trips to the bin.

A 16 gallon tank is heavy when full of water, and the vac takes up floor space. Peak horsepower is higher than most models here, though suction depends on the hose and filter. Against the 9 gallon CRAFTSMAN, it holds nearly twice as much. Against the DEWALT, it has a bigger tank at a lower tier.

Empty the tank on a drain or outside after wet jobs. Remove the filter before sucking up liquid, unless the maker says otherwise. For a big wet job, a drain port or a garden hose connection saves lifting a heavy full tank to empty it.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN CMXEVBE17590 9 gallon 4.25 peak HP wet dry shop vacuum, general purpose
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN 9 gallon vac has a 4.25 peak horsepower motor and a general purpose design. It is the value alternative to the DEWALT and a sensible size for home garages.

A 9 gallon tank covers a car interior, a workshop floor or a small spill, and the vac is light enough to carry up stairs. The peak horsepower figure is lower than the DEWALT, though real suction differences are smaller than the numbers suggest. Against the DEWALT, it lacks the blower port in this listing and costs less. Against the 16 gallon CRAFTSMAN, it is more portable.

Empty the tank after each use and check the filter. Replace the filter when suction drops. Because the tank is a manageable size, it is easy to carry up to a car or onto a deck for quick jobs.

products.name: Vacmaster Professional Beast Series VFB511H 5 gallon 5.5 peak HP wet dry vac
products.description:
The Vacmaster Beast Series is a 5 gallon wet dry vac with a 5.5 peak horsepower motor, packing high power in a compact tank. It is a more professional range of Vacmaster's line.

A smaller tank is easier to carry and store and fills faster, so it suits car detailing, workshop spot cleaning and quick jobs. The peak figure is higher than the DEWALT, but the tank is only about half the size. Against the Vacmaster VOC507PF, it has more power. Against the Shop-Vac 8 gallon, it is more compact.

Empty the tank often and clean the filter. Use a bag for fine dust. The small tank is an advantage when you want a vac you can store under a bench and pull out in seconds.

products.name: Shop-Vac 5922805 8 gallon 4.5 peak HP wet dry vacuum with blower, 1.25 inch x 7 ft hose
products.description:
The Shop-Vac 8 gallon vac has a 4.5 peak horsepower motor, a blower function and a 1.25 inch by 7 foot hose. It is a classic garage vac from the brand that popularised the category.

A 1.25 inch hose is a standard size and suits general cleanup, though a wider hose moves larger debris better. The blower port helps with leaves and drying. Against the DEWALT 9 gallon, it is slightly smaller and cheaper. Against the Stanley, it has a blower.

Empty the tank and check the filter. Use a foam sleeve for wet jobs if the maker recommends it. A foam sleeve over the filter is a cheap way to protect it during wet pickup, if the maker approves it.

products.name: Stanley SL18116P 6 gallon 4 horsepower wet dry vacuum, black
products.description:
The Stanley SL18116P is a 6 gallon wet dry vac with a 4 horsepower motor listed, a simple, no frills machine at a low tier. It handles car interiors, small workshop messes and light spills.

Six gallons is a good middle size for a home, small enough to store and big enough to avoid constant emptying. Against the Armor All 2.5 gallon, it is bigger, and against the DEWALT, it has fewer features. The listing gives few details, so rely on basic expectations.

Empty it after use and check the filter. Replace the filter when suction drops. Treat the Stanley as a household helper for the car and the garage floor rather than a tool for daily trade use.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Tank size sets how long you can work before emptying. A 2.5 gallon vac suits a car, a 6 to 9 gallon vac suits a garage and a 16 gallon vac suits a workshop or flooded basement. A bigger tank is heavier and takes more space, so choose for your typical job. The usual buyer mistake is buying on the horsepower number and ignoring the hose, which limits real airflow.

Peak horsepower is measured with no load and is a marketing figure, as listed from 2 on the Armor All to 6.5 on the CRAFTSMAN 16 gallon. Real suction comes from airflow in cubic feet per minute and water lift, which listings rarely state. Use horsepower only to compare roughly within a brand. Think about where you will store the vac, since a big one is awkward to move and a small one fits on a shelf.

A wider hose moves more air and larger debris. Many shop vacs use a 1.25 inch hose, as the Shop-Vac listing states, and wider hoses of 2 to 2.5 inches handle sawdust and chunks better. A narrow hose clogs more easily. Check that the power cord is long enough to reach around a garage without an extension.

Filters protect the motor and the air. Cartridge filters trap fine dust, but they must be removed or covered for wet pickup. Fine dust like drywall clogs filters quickly, and bags help. A HEPA filter is a different system and often a separate accessory. Look at the wheels, because small casters stick on rough concrete and big ones roll more easily.

A blower port, as on the DEWALT and Shop-Vac, lets you blow leaves and dust. A set of attachments, such as a floor tool, crevice tool and extension wands, makes a shop vac more useful. Check what is in the box. Consider the noise, as shop vacs are loud and a quieter model is nicer in an enclosed space.

Casters, a drain port and a strong latch make a vac easier to live with. Plastic tanks dent and crack, and steel tanks are heavier but tougher. A tank you can empty easily gets used more. If you will use it with a power tool, check whether the hose and port match the tool's dust connection.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tanks from 2.5 to 16 gallons and typical garage and car jobs. We favoured a good fit between tank and use. We did not run suction tests. Owner feedback patterns about filter clogging, lid latches and cord length shaped our scoring.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at peak horsepower from 2 to 6.5 and treated it as marketing. Where airflow data was missing we used rough comparisons. We treated peak horsepower as a marketing number and did not use it as a ranking criterion.

howWeEvaluated.title: Hose and filter
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered hose diameters, filter types and bag options. Better filtration and wider hoses scored higher. Where a listing gave a hose diameter we used it as a signal of real airflow.

howWeEvaluated.title: Features
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed blower ports, attachments and drain ports. Useful features scored higher. We compared accessories included and noted when a blower port was available.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed build quality, filter cost and owner feedback patterns about clogging and latch failure. Established brands scored higher on parts. Tank construction was compared across the seven models.

cards.label: Small tank
cards.text: The Armor All, Vacmaster Beast and Stanley are light and easy to store. They fill quickly.

cards.label: Large tank
cards.text: The CRAFTSMAN 16 gallon and DEWALT 9 gallon last longer between emptying. They are heavier and bulkier.

howToChoose.note: Choose small for car and bench use and large for garages and workshops.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A fine dust filter or bag, a wide hose, a tank that empties easily and ideally a dust port to connect to tools.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The DEWALT and CRAFTSMAN vacs offer solid filter support, and a wider hose is a worthwhile upgrade.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You use it daily or on a job site. The DEWALT or CRAFTSMAN 16 gallon are built for it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You vacuum a car or a garage occasionally. The Stanley or Armor All are enough.

Wet debris smells and rusts. Empty and dry the tank.

maintenance.why: A wet cartridge clogs and tears. Use a foam sleeve if the maker allows.
Cracked hoses lose suction. Replace damaged parts.
Dust and moisture build up in seams. A damp cloth keeps them clean.

faq.a: Not much. It is measured with no load and does not predict real suction. Hose size, filter and airflow matter more. Many owners say that a second cartridge filter, kept clean and ready, saves a lot of waiting when the first one clogs.

faq.q: What tank size should I buy?
faq.a: A 2.5 gallon vac suits a car, a 6 to 9 gallon vac suits a garage and a 16 gallon vac suits a large workshop. Use a bag for drywall dust and ash, since a filter alone will clog fast.
Yes, with a wet dry vac, but remove the dry filter if the maker advises. Empty the tank after wet jobs. Do not vacuum hot embers, flammable liquids or fine dust like toner without a suitable machine.
For fine dust like drywall, yes, because it protects the filter. For general debris, a filter alone is fine. Keep the cord clear of the hose, as stepping on it can damage the cord.

faq.q: Can I use it as a blower?
faq.a: Models with a blower port, such as the DEWALT and Shop-Vac, can. They are weaker than a dedicated leaf blower. Empty the tank outside to avoid kicking up dust in the garage.

faq.q: How do I stop the filter clogging?
faq.a: Use a bag, tap the filter after use and avoid sucking up fine dust without protection. Clean the float valve if the vac stops picking up water, because a stuck float cuts off the motor.
